Opaque handle type for the libsepol API, referenced here for messaging/debug facilities. It is not defined in this header; only used as a parameter type.

Opaque handle type for libsepol operations. This header only references it; the actual definition is not present here and is expected to be provided by <sepol/handle.h>. Details such as lifetime management and fields are unknown in this file.

Opaque policy database type representing a loaded SELinux policy. This header only references it; the actual definition is not present here and is expected to be provided by <sepol/policydb.h>. Details are unknown in this file.

Opaque context record type encapsulating an SELinux security context (user:role:type[:mls]). This header only references it; the actual definition is not present here and is expected to be provided by <sepol/context_record.h>. Details are unknown in this file.

Opaque libsepol handle used to carry error reporting and configuration state across API calls. It is referenced here but defined elsewhere (sepol/handle.h).
Opaque SELinux policy database object. This header only references it; definition is external (sepol/policydb.h).
Opaque handle type used by libsepol API calls. It is referenced here but not defined in this header; definition is in another header (sepol/handle.h). No further details are available in this file.

Handle object used by libsepol APIs for error reporting and configuration. Only referenced here; its definition is not present in this header.

Opaque type representing a declaration of AV rules, identified by a declaration ID. The concrete structure is not defined in this header.

typedef struct avtab_key {
	uint16_t source_type;
	uint16_t target_type;
	uint16_t target_class;
#define AVTAB_ALLOWED		0x0001
#define AVTAB_AUDITALLOW	0x0002
#define AVTAB_AUDITDENY		0x0004
#define AVTAB_NEVERALLOW	0x0080
#define AVTAB_AV		(AVTAB_ALLOWED | AVTAB_AUDITALLOW | AVTAB_AUDITDENY)
#define AVTAB_TRANSITION	0x0010
#define AVTAB_MEMBER		0x0020
#define AVTAB_CHANGE		0x0040
#define AVTAB_TYPE		(AVTAB_TRANSITION | AVTAB_MEMBER | AVTAB_CHANGE)
#define AVTAB_XPERMS_ALLOWED	0x0100
#define AVTAB_XPERMS_AUDITALLOW	0x0200
#define AVTAB_XPERMS_DONTAUDIT	0x0400
#define AVTAB_XPERMS_NEVERALLOW	0x0800
#define AVTAB_XPERMS		(AVTAB_XPERMS_ALLOWED | AVTAB_XPERMS_AUDITALLOW | AVTAB_XPERMS_DONTAUDIT)
#define AVTAB_ENABLED_OLD	0x80000000
#define AVTAB_ENABLED		0x8000	/* reserved for used in cond_avtab */
	uint16_t specified;	/* what fields are specified */
} avtab_key_t;
objects.description: Key for avtab entries: identifies a rule by source type, target type, target class, and flags in specified indicating which rule categories apply. Macros define bit masks for rule types and xperms. Used as the hash key.

Extended permissions blob associated with an avtab datum, supporting ioctl or netlink message granular permissions. 'specified' selects xperms class; 'driver' further qualifies; 'perms' is a bitmap array.
Payload stored in avtab for a given key. 'data' encodes the access vector bits or a type value; optional xperms points to extended permissions.

objects.definition: typedef struct avtab_node *avtab_ptr_t;
objects.description: Alias typedef for a pointer to avtab_node, used for hash buckets and linkage. Note: this is itself a pointer type; the ptr_type here is avtab_ptr_t *, i.e., pointer to the alias.
Linked-list node used in hash buckets of avtab. Contains a key, datum, next pointer, and auxiliary parse/merge flags used by the parser/writer only.
Hash table of access vector/type rules. htable is an array of bucket heads (avtab_ptr_t), with nel element count, nslot number of buckets, and mask for hashing.

Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) conditional expression node used by the SELinux policydb. Each node represents an operator or operand with expr_type indicating the token, boolean referencing a policy boolean symbol index, and next linking to the next token in the RPN list.
Singly linked list of avtab entries associated with a conditional block, representing rules to enable/disable based on a condition's value.

Represents a conditional block (if/else) in a policy. Holds the expression, current evaluation state, rule lists for true/false branches, parsing-time avrule lists, bookkeeping for unique booleans and precomputed outcomes, linkage to next cond node, and flags (e.g., tunable).

objects.definition:
typedef struct constraint_expr {
#define CEXPR_NOT		1	/* not expr */
#define CEXPR_AND		2	/* expr and expr */
#define CEXPR_OR		3	/* expr or expr */
#define CEXPR_ATTR		4	/* attr op attr */
#define CEXPR_NAMES		5	/* attr op names */
	uint32_t expr_type;	/* expression type */

#define CEXPR_USER 1		/* user */
#define CEXPR_ROLE 2		/* role */
#define CEXPR_TYPE 4		/* type */
#define CEXPR_TARGET 8		/* target if set, source otherwise */
#define CEXPR_XTARGET 16	/* special 3rd target for validatetrans rule */
#define CEXPR_L1L2 32		/* low level 1 vs. low level 2 */
#define CEXPR_L1H2 64		/* low level 1 vs. high level 2 */
#define CEXPR_H1L2 128		/* high level 1 vs. low level 2 */
#define CEXPR_H1H2 256		/* high level 1 vs. high level 2 */
#define CEXPR_L1H1 512		/* low level 1 vs. high level 1 */
#define CEXPR_L2H2 1024		/* low level 2 vs. high level 2 */
	uint32_t attr;		/* attribute */

#define CEXPR_EQ     1		/* == or eq */
#define CEXPR_NEQ    2		/* != */
#define CEXPR_DOM    3		/* dom */
#define CEXPR_DOMBY  4		/* domby  */
#define CEXPR_INCOMP 5		/* incomp */
	uint32_t op;		/* operator */

	ebitmap_t names;	/* names */
	struct type_set *type_names;

	struct constraint_expr *next;	/* next expression */
} constraint_expr_t;
objects.description: Represents a node in a SELinux policy constraint boolean expression. Each node encodes the expression type (logical ops or attribute comparisons), attribute kind (user/role/type and level selectors), operator, and referenced name/type sets. Nodes form a singly linked list via next to build an expression tree in list form. Uses ebitmap_t for name sets and optionally a referenced type_set (forward-declared elsewhere).

Represents a constraint applied to a set of permissions in SELinux policy. Each node lists the affected access vector permissions and a pointer to the constraint expression to evaluate. Nodes can be chained via next to represent multiple constraints.

Represents a SELinux security context containing user, role, type identifiers, and an MLS range. It is the internal context representation used by the security server. The MLS portion is managed via mls_range_t utilities from mls_types.h.
Node in an extensible bitmap linked list. Each node stores a MAPTYPE-sized chunk of bits starting at startbit and points to the next node. Used internally to represent sparse/segmented bitmaps.

Extensible bitmap type implemented as a linked list of ebitmap_node_t segments. Provides operations for set logic, bit access, iteration, and lifecycle management via the declared API functions. highbit tracks the highest position in the total bitmap that is relevant.
Opaque handle type for libsepol operations. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Opaque policy database object used by libsepol to represent SELinux policy. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Standard fixed-width unsigned 32-bit integer typedef from stdint.h. Only referenced; not defined here.
Expanded bitmap structure used in libsepol for sets of integers such as types/roles. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Represents a set of types (and possibly attributes) in SELinux policy semantics. Only referenced; not defined here.
Represents a set of roles in SELinux policy semantics. Only referenced; not defined here.
Semantic representation of an MLS level (category/classification expressions). Only referenced; not defined here.
Concrete MLS level (expanded form). Only referenced; not defined here.
Semantic representation of an MLS range. Only referenced; not defined here.
Concrete MLS range (expanded form). Only referenced; not defined here.
Access vector rule structure in SELinux policy. Only referenced; not defined here.
Access vector table structure used to store AV rules. Only referenced; not defined here.
List node structure for conditional AV rules. Only referenced; not defined here.

objects.definition:
typedef char *sepol_security_context_t;
typedef const char *sepol_const_security_context_t;
objects.description: Pointer-typed string representing a security context; variable-length NUL-terminated text encoding of security attributes per SELinux/Flask policy. The const alias indicates read-only contexts. Storage lifetime and allocation are not defined here; callers typically manage memory or receive buffers from other APIs.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t sepol_access_vector_t;
objects.description: 32-bit bitmask representing an access vector (AV). Bits correspond to permissions whose meaning depends on the object class in policy.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t sepol_security_class_t;
objects.description: 16-bit identifier for an SELinux/Flask object class. SEPOL_SECCLASS_NULL (0) denotes no class.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t sepol_security_id_t;
objects.description: 32-bit security identifier (SID). SEPOL_SECSID_NULL (0) denotes the null/invalid SID.

Decision result for an access vector check between a pair of SIDs and a class. Contains bitmasks of allowed and decided permissions, audit allow/deny masks, and a sequence number (policy sequence). No constructors/destructors defined here; it is a plain aggregate.

objects.definition: typedef char *hashtab_key_t;
objects.description: Generic key type used by the hash table API. Represents a mutable C-string pointer used as the key in entries.

objects.definition: typedef const char *const_hashtab_key_t;
objects.description: Generic constant key type used for read-only key operations in the hash table API.

objects.definition: typedef void *hashtab_datum_t;
objects.description: Generic datum/value type stored in the hash table. Opaque to the table; ownership and lifetime are managed by the caller.

objects.definition: typedef struct hashtab_node *hashtab_ptr_t;
objects.description: Pointer alias to a hash table node structure. Used for chaining within buckets and for the table storage type.
Node in a hash table bucket chain, storing a key, datum, and next pointer for collision chaining.
Concrete hash table container holding the bucket array, size, element count, and user-supplied hash and key-compare callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef hashtab_val_t *hashtab_t;
objects.description: Public handle type for a hash table instance (pointer to hashtab_val_t).

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares the function link_modules and references external types from other headers (sepol_handle_t and policydb_t). Therefore, there are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to extract.

MLS level consisting of a sensitivity (sens) and a bitmap of categories (cat). Used as the atomic label component and building block of ranges. Functions in this header allow init, copy, destroy, equality, dominance, and comparison semantics.

Closed MLS range defined by a low and high level. Provides helpers to init, destroy, copy, equality test, containment, and to compute a greatest lower bound / least upper bound overlap (glb/lub) via mls_range_glblub.
Semantic representation of a contiguous range of category bits, organized as a singly linked list via next. Used to parse or hold textual category sets before bitmap compilation.

Semantic representation of an MLS level with a sensitivity and a linked-list of category ranges (mls_semantic_cat_t). Typically used during parsing and translation before conversion to ebitmap-based mls_level_t.
Semantic representation of an MLS range comprised of low and high semantic levels. Complementary to mls_range_t during parsing/serialization stages.

A container for a SELinux module package, holding a policy database pointer and associated ancillary content blobs (file_contexts, seusers, user_extra, netfilter_contexts) with their lengths and a module/package version. The exact semantics of each blob are determined by SELinux tooling; memory ownership and lifecycle are managed by callers of this API.

enum {
	POLICYDB_CAP_NETPEER,
	POLICYDB_CAP_OPENPERM,
	POLICYDB_CAP_EXTSOCKCLASS,
	POLICYDB_CAP_ALWAYSNETWORK,
	POLICYDB_CAP_CGROUPSECLABEL,
	POLICYDB_CAP_NNP_NOSUID_TRANSITION,
	POLICYDB_CAP_GENFS_SECLABEL_SYMLINKS,
	POLICYDB_CAP_IOCTL_SKIP_CLOEXEC,
	POLICYDB_CAP_USERSPACE_INITIAL_CONTEXT,
	POLICYDB_CAP_NETLINK_XPERM,
	POLICYDB_CAP_NETIF_WILDCARD,
	POLICYDB_CAP_GENFS_SECLABEL_WILDCARD,
	POLICYDB_CAP_FUNCTIONFS_SECLABEL,
	POLICYDB_CAP_MEMFD_CLASS,
	__POLICYDB_CAP_MAX
};
#define POLICYDB_CAP_MAX (__POLICYDB_CAP_MAX - 1)
objects.description: Anonymous enumeration defining numeric constants for SELinux policy capabilities. Since the enum is unnamed, its type is the implicit anonymous enum type; the constants (e.g., POLICYDB_CAP_NETPEER) are integer macros/identifiers. POLICYDB_CAP_MAX macro provides the highest valid capability index. No storage-owning structures are defined here.
Represents a set of types along with a negated subset and flags indicating wildcard or complement semantics, used in policy rules (e.g., attributes, ~, *).
Represents a set of roles with flags supporting wildcard and complement semantics, used in role-related rules.
Symbol table datum for an individual permission identifier.
Represents a common permission set that multiple classes may share as a prefix.
Describes a security class: links to common permissions, class-specific permissions, constraints, validate_trans rules, and defaulting behavior for new objects.
Datum for a role or role attribute, including dominance relationships, authorized types, and bounds.
Linked list node describing a concrete role transition (current role+type+class -> new role) in compiled policy.
Linked list entry granting permission for role changes (role -> new_role).
Key for filename-based type transition mapping: target type, class, and basename.
Value for filename transition table: set of source types, resulting object type, and chaining pointer.
Symbol datum for a type, type attribute, or alias, including expansion maps, flags, and bounds.
Symbol datum for a user, including authorized roles, MLS range and defaults, caches, and bounds.
Represents a sensitivity level datum with optional aliasing and a flag used during policy checking.
Symbol datum for a category with an alias flag.
Key triple for MLS range transition mappings (source type, target type, target class).
Symbol datum for a conditional boolean or tunable, with current state and flags.
Linked list node of class-specific data (permissions or resulting type) used by rules.
Holds extended permission bitmaps (e.g., ioctl function/driver, netlink msg) for AV rules.
Represents a high-level policy rule (allow/audit/deny/type transition/xperms), including type sets, class/perm lists, metadata, and linkage.
Declarative role transition rule used in modules, before compilation to concrete role_trans entries.
Declarative rule allowing role changes to any of a set of new roles.
Declarative filename-based type transition rule (with optional self flag), linking basename, class, and resulting type.
Declarative MLS range transition rule for sets of source/target types and classes, yielding a semantic range.
Stores object-context mappings for various kinds (initial SIDs, fs, ports, netifs, nodes, genfs), including contexts/SIDs and linked list chaining.
Represents a list of genfs context specifications for a given filesystem type.
Holds bitmaps of which symbols are in scope for a given declaration and a per-class permission map.
A branch of policy declarations containing TE/RBAC statements, conditional rules, per-branch symbol tables, and links to next branch.
Represents an optional/conditional block with multiple branches of avrule declarations and a pointer to the enabled one.
Records whether a symbol is required or declared in a decl and which declaration IDs reference it.
Top-level in-memory representation of a SELinux policy, including symbol tables, rules, contexts, indexes, and feature/version info.
Wrapper structure embedding a policydb, used for API separation. No dedicated constructors in this header.
Represents a policy input/output source (memory buffer or stdio file) with metadata and handle pointer.
Wrapper embedding a policy_file for API namespacing. No constructors here.

Opaque/forward-declared struct representing an SELinux access vector decision result. It is referenced as an output parameter to hold allow/deny bits and related metadata, but this header does not provide the definition. Details of its fields are unknown from this file.

Node in the SID table’s hash chains. Holds a single security identifier (SID), its associated security context, and a pointer to the next node in the bucket list. Used internally to implement the hash table buckets.

objects.definition: typedef struct sidtab_node *sidtab_ptr_t;
objects.description: Alias type for a pointer to sidtab_node_t; in this header it is primarily used as the element type of the hash table array (htable) inside sidtab_t.

Security identifier table: a hash table mapping sepol_security_id_t values to security contexts. Contains the bucket array (htable), element count (nel), next SID allocator (next_sid), and a shutdown flag. Lifecycle is managed via sepol_sidtab_init and sepol_sidtab_destroy; population and queries via the provided API functions.
Common header for all symbol-table datum types. Must be the first field of any struct stored in a symtab so those structs can be cast to this type. Holds a 1-based identifier (0 is never valid).
Symbol table that maps strings to datum values using an underlying hashtab. Tracks the number of primary names inserted. The table field owns/manages the internal hash table from the hashtab API.
Referenced SELinux policy database type brought in via include; not defined in this header. Per instructions, types merely referenced are ignored. No custom types are defined in this header.

functions.name: sepol_set_policydb_from_file
functions.description: Sets libsepol’s internal policy database (policydb) from the contents of the provided file stream, so that subsequent service calls can operate using that policy. Typical usage is to open a SELinux policy file and pass its FILE* here before calling other libsepol functions that require an initialized policydb. Exact success/failure return conventions and the expected policy format version are not specified in this header; details are inferred from the name and comment and may depend on the libsepol build/version.
requirements: fp must not be NULL (inferred from pointer parameter usage).
fp must be an open, readable FILE* stream (inferred from reading a policy from a file).
The file content must be a valid SELinux policy database in the format expected by libsepol; exact format/version details are unknown from this header (inferred from function purpose).
Call this before invoking service calls that rely on an initialized internal policydb, as implied by the comment (“for subsequent service calls”).

Callers must check the function’s int return value to detect failure; specific conventions (e.g., 0 on success, <0 on error) are not stated in this header and are therefore unknown; consult libsepol documentation or implementation.

functions.name: sepol_policy_file_create
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new sepol_policy_file_t object. Intended as the first step before configuring the policy file to point to memory or a FILE for subsequent reads/writes.
requirements: pf must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sepol_policy_file_t* (inferred from signature).
On success, *pf will be set to a valid policy file object; caller is responsible for later calling sepol_policy_file_free on it (inferred from paired free).
Return value should be checked; nonzero indicates failure (inferred from int return type and common pattern).

functions.name: sepol_policy_file_free
functions.description: Release all resources associated with a sepol_policy_file_t created by sepol_policy_file_create.
requirements: pf should be a pointer previously returned via sepol_policy_file_create (inferred from pairing).

functions.description: Initializes an avtab_t instance to a valid empty state. Call this before any other operations on the table (e.g., allocation, insert, read). Typically sets internal counters and pointers to defaults.
requirements: The avtab_t* argument must be a valid, writable pointer.
The avtab_t instance must not already own allocated resources unless the implementation supports re-init (unknown).
Check the integer return value: nonzero likely indicates failure (exact convention unknown).

functions.name: avtab_alloc
functions.description: Allocates internal storage (hash table buckets) for an avtab_t. The second parameter controls the table sizing (number of slots/buckets or a size hint). Use after avtab_init and before inserting entries.
requirements: The avtab_t* must point to an avtab previously initialized by avtab_init.

The size hint must be within implementation limits; the header defines MAX_AVTAB_SIZE and related hash bucket limits; callers should not request more than MAX_AVTAB_SIZE (inferred from comments and macros).
On failure, the function returns a nonzero error code (exact convention unknown); callers must check the return value.
Do not use the table for insert/search if allocation fails.

functions.name: avtab_insert
functions.signature: int avtab_insert(avtab_t * h, avtab_key_t * k, avtab_datum_t * d);
functions.description: Inserts a key/datum pair into the access vector table. Fails or overwrites depending on existing entries and uniqueness rules (details not documented here). Intended for standard unique inserts.
requirements: h must reference an initialized and allocated avtab_t.
k and d must be non-null pointers to fully-initialized structures.
avtab_key_t fields (source_type, target_type, target_class) must be set to valid identifiers; k->specified must contain appropriate AVTAB_* bits for the datum (inferred).
If insertion fails (e.g., duplicate not allowed), a nonzero error is returned; callers must check the return value.
Behavior on duplicate keys is not guaranteed by this header; use avtab_insert_nonunique if duplicates are expected.

functions.name: avtab_search
functions.description: Looks up a key in the table and returns a pointer to the associated avtab_datum_t if found, or NULL otherwise.
requirements: h must reference an initialized (and typically allocated/populated) avtab_t.
k must be non-null and contain initialized fields matching the target entry; k->specified should correspond to the desired selector bits (inferred).
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by the table; callers must not free it and must not mutate it unless the API guarantees mutability (unknown).

functions.name: avtab_destroy
functions.description: Releases all resources held by the avtab, including hash buckets and any stored nodes/extended-perms. Leaves the avtab_t in a destroyed state.
requirements: h must be a valid pointer to an avtab_t previously initialized/allocated.
After destroy, the table must not be used unless reinitialized.
All outstanding pointers to table entries become invalid after this call.

functions.name: avtab_map
functions.signature: int avtab_map(const avtab_t * h, int (*apply)(avtab_key_t * k, avtab_datum_t * d, void *args), void *args);
functions.description: Iterates over all entries in the table and invokes the user-supplied callback for each (key, datum) pair, passing through the user args. Useful for enumeration, validation, or transformation.
requirements: h must refer to a valid, initialized table; it may be empty.
apply must be a non-null function pointer with the declared signature.
The callback may be called many times; it must be reentrant with respect to its own state and must not free or structurally modify the table unless the implementation explicitly allows it (unknown).
The meaning of the callback return value and how it affects iteration is not documented here (unknown); callers should be prepared for avtab_map to return an int status and must check it.

functions.name: avtab_hash_eval
functions.description: Evaluates and reports (e.g., logs/prints) hash distribution statistics for the table, using tag to label the output. Intended for diagnostics and tuning.
requirements: h must point to a valid, initialized table (preferably populated).
tag should be a valid NUL-terminated string; whether NULL is allowed is not specified (unknown).
This function produces side effects via diagnostics; there is no return value to check.

functions.name: avtab_read_item
functions.signature: int avtab_read_item(struct policy_file *fp, uint32_t vers, avtab_t * a, int (*insert)(avtab_t * a, avtab_key_t * k, avtab_datum_t * d, void *p), void *p);
functions.description: Reads a single avtab entry from a policy file stream according to the specified policy version, then inserts it into the provided table by invoking the supplied insert callback. Used by policy loaders during parse/deserialization.
requirements: fp must be a valid pointer to an open/initialized policy_file for reading.
vers must be a supported policy version for the encoded data (exact valid range unknown).
a must be an initialized (and typically allocated) avtab_t ready to receive entries.
insert must be a non-null callback matching the declared signature; it will be called with the table, a parsed key, datum, and the user pointer p.
The user pointer p is passed through untouched; it may be NULL if the callback accepts NULL.
Callers must check the returned int status for success/failure and handle I/O or format errors.

functions.name: avtab_read
functions.signature: int avtab_read(avtab_t * a, struct policy_file *fp, uint32_t vers);
functions.description: Reads and populates an entire avtab from a policy file stream using the specified policy version. Effectively deserializes the table from the file.
requirements: a must be initialized (and allocated as required by implementation) prior to reading.
fp must point to an open/initialized policy_file positioned appropriately for reading the avtab data.
vers must be a supported policy version (exact range unknown).
On error (I/O, format, version mismatch), a nonzero status is returned; callers must check and handle the return value.

functions.name: avtab_insert_nonunique
functions.signature: avtab_ptr_t avtab_insert_nonunique(avtab_t * h, avtab_key_t * key, avtab_datum_t * datum);
functions.description: Inserts a key/datum pair even if an entry with the same key already exists, and returns a pointer to the newly inserted node. Enables multiple nodes per key (non-unique keys).
requirements: h must be an initialized and allocated table.
key and datum must be non-null and fully initialized.
The returned avtab_ptr_t is a pointer to an internal node owned by the table; callers must not free it and must not use it after table mutation or destruction unless guaranteed safe (unknown).

functions.name: avtab_insert_with_parse_context
functions.signature: avtab_ptr_t avtab_insert_with_parse_context(avtab_t * h, avtab_key_t * key, avtab_datum_t * datum, void *parse_context);
functions.description: Inserts a key/datum pair and associates an opaque parse_context pointer with the created node (useful for parsers to track source location or metadata). Returns the inserted node pointer.
requirements: h must be an initialized and allocated table.
key and datum must be non-null and initialized.
parse_context is an arbitrary pointer passed through and stored; its lifetime must outlive any use via the node while the table exists (inferred).
The returned node pointer is owned by the table and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: avtab_search_node
functions.description: Searches for a node matching the given key and returns a pointer to the first matching avtab_node, or NULL if none exists. Use with avtab_search_node_next to iterate over multiple nodes for non-unique keys.
requirements: h must refer to an initialized table.
key must be non-null and initialized; key->specified should indicate the type of entry being searched (inferred).
The returned node pointer is internal to the table; do not free it and avoid mutating it unless the API guarantees safety (unknown).

functions.name: avtab_search_node_next
functions.description: Continues iteration over nodes that match the search criteria, starting from the given node, returning the next matching node or NULL. The specified parameter filters entries by the specified bitmask (e.g., AVTAB_*).
requirements: node must be either a valid node returned by avtab_search_node/previous avtab_search_node_next call, or NULL to indicate no further iteration.
specified should be set to the desired AVTAB_* mask to match while iterating; valid values are from the AVTAB_* constants defined in the header (inferred).
Returned node pointer is owned by the table; do not free it.

functions.name: cond_evaluate_expr
functions.signature: extern int cond_evaluate_expr(policydb_t * p, cond_expr_t * expr);
functions.description: Evaluates a conditional expression (reverse polish notation) within the context of a policy database. Intended to compute the truth value of the expression for enabling/disabling conditional rules. Usage: pass a valid, initialized policydb_t and a linked-list expression rooted at expr; use the returned int to determine evaluation result and/or error.
requirements: p must point to a valid, initialized policydb_t (e.g., created/loaded prior to evaluation).
expr must be a valid expression list (nodes correctly linked and with expr_type values in [COND_BOOL..COND_LAST]).
The expression depth should not exceed COND_EXPR_MAXDEPTH (10).
The number of unique booleans referenced during evaluation should not exceed COND_MAX_BOOLS (5) if precomputation is expected; behavior beyond that is library-defined.
Callers must check the int return value for success/failure; exact codes are library-defined.

functions.name: cond_copy_expr
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of a conditional expression list. Useful when duplicating conditional blocks or preserving original expressions during transformations.
requirements: expr must be either NULL or a pointer to a valid, well-formed cond_expr_t linked list.
If non-NULL is returned, the caller owns the returned copy and must later free it with cond_expr_destroy().
On failure, NULL may be returned; callers must check the return pointer before use.

functions.name: cond_expr_equal
functions.signature: extern int cond_expr_equal(cond_node_t * a, cond_node_t * b);
functions.description: Compares the conditional expressions of two cond_node_t nodes for equivalence. Intended to detect duplicate or identical conditional blocks.
requirements: a and b must be non-NULL pointers to valid cond_node_t objects with expr fields set appropriately.
Only expression equality is implied by the name; equality of rule lists or other fields is not guaranteed.
Callers must check the int return value to determine equality vs. error; exact values are library-defined.

functions.name: cond_normalize_expr
functions.signature: extern int cond_normalize_expr(policydb_t * p, cond_node_t * cn);
functions.description: Normalizes/optimizes the expression in the given cond_node (e.g., canonicalization, precomputation indexes). Intended to prepare expressions for evaluation or comparison.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t.
cn must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid cond_node_t with a well-formed expr list.
Normalization may depend on policy booleans and limits like COND_MAX_BOOLS; callers must check the return value for success.

functions.name: cond_node_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a cond_node and releases associated resources (expression, lists, and internal state as applicable). Safe cleanup helper.
requirements: node must either be NULL or point to a cond_node_t previously allocated/initialized by the library (e.g., via cond_node_create or parsing).
After destruction, the pointer becomes invalid; do not reuse it.
Caller must ensure no other data structures retain references to internals freed by this call.

functions.name: cond_expr_destroy
functions.description: Frees an entire conditional expression linked list starting at expr.
requirements: expr may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid list allocated by the library or compatible allocator.
After destruction, expr and its nodes must not be accessed.

functions.name: cond_node_find
functions.description: Finds an equivalent cond_node in a haystack list or inserts/creates one in the policy context if absent. Returns the found or newly created node and indicates via was_created whether a new node was created.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t.
needle must be a valid cond_node_t whose expression (and possibly metadata) identify the desired node.
haystack must be a valid list head or NULL if no list is provided.
was_created may be NULL if the caller does not need creation status; if non-NULL it must point to writable int storage.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect failure.

functions.name: cond_node_create
functions.description: Creates a new cond_node in the policy context, optionally using fields from the provided template node. Returns a pointer to the created node.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t.
node may be NULL or a pointer to a partially-populated cond_node_t used as a template; required fields (if any) are library-defined and not specified here.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL and later destroy the node with cond_node_destroy() when no longer needed.

functions.name: cond_node_search
functions.signature:
extern cond_node_t *cond_node_search(policydb_t * p, cond_node_t * list,
				     cond_node_t * cn);
functions.description: Searches for a cond_node equivalent to cn within the provided list in the context of the policy. Returns the matching node or NULL if not found.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t.
list must be a valid cond_node_t list head (or NULL for empty).
cn must be a valid cond_node_t with comparable expression/identity fields populated.
Caller must handle a NULL return as "not found" or error depending on context.

functions.name: evaluate_conds
functions.description: Evaluates all conditional blocks in the policy database and updates rule activation state accordingly. Typically called after policy load or when booleans change.
requirements: p must be a valid, fully-initialized policydb_t with conditional nodes linked in.
Evaluation may depend on boolean indices (see cond_init_bool_indexes); call ordering may matter relative to initialization.
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cond_av_list_search
functions.description: Searches a conditional access vector list for a rule matching the provided avtab key. Returns the associated avtab_datum_t if found.
requirements: key must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid avtab_key_t identifying the rule to search.
cond_list must be a valid cond_av_list_t list (or NULL for empty).
Caller must handle a NULL return as "not found" or error depending on context.

functions.name: cond_av_list_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a conditional AV list and releases list node resources. Intended for cleanup after parsing or module handling.
requirements: list may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid list created/owned by the caller context.
After destruction, list nodes must not be accessed.

functions.name: cond_optimize_lists
functions.description: Optimizes internal conditional lists associated with the provided cond_list_t, potentially deduplicating or restructuring rules for efficiency. Exact transformations are library-defined.
requirements: cl must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid cond_list_t container produced by the library (e.g., during parsing or module processing).
Caller should not rely on list node addresses remaining stable after optimization.

functions.name: cond_policydb_init
functions.description: Initializes conditional-related state in a policydb_t. Should be called before using conditional features on a newly created or loaded policy database that lacks initialization.
requirements: p must be a non-NULL pointer to a policydb_t to initialize.
Must be called before operations that assume initialized conditional state (e.g., cond_init_bool_indexes, evaluate_conds).
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cond_policydb_destroy
functions.description: Releases conditional-related state stored in a policydb_t. Cleanup counterpart to cond_policydb_init.
requirements: p may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a policydb_t previously initialized for conditional use.
After destruction, conditional-specific members of p must not be accessed until reinitialized.

functions.name: cond_list_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a list of conditional nodes/structures referred to by cond_list_t. Cleanup helper after parsing or module processing.
requirements: list may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid cond_list_t allocated/managed by the library.
After destruction, the list must not be accessed.

functions.name: cond_init_bool_indexes
functions.description: Initializes boolean indices and mappings within the policy database to support efficient conditional evaluation and precomputation (limited by COND_MAX_BOOLS).
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t with boolean symbols loaded.
Should be called before evaluate_conds() if boolean indices are required.
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cond_destroy_bool
functions.signature: extern int cond_destroy_bool(hashtab_key_t key, hashtab_datum_t datum, void *p);
functions.description: Callback/utility to destroy a boolean entry in a hashtable, freeing resources associated with a policy boolean. Intended for use with table iteration/destruction.
requirements: key and datum must be pointers compatible with the hashtable’s expected key/datum types for booleans.
p is an opaque caller context pointer; if used, it must be valid per the calling hashtable routine.
Return value semantics are library/hashtable-defined; callers should propagate or check as required.

functions.name: cond_index_bool
functions.signature:
extern int cond_index_bool(hashtab_key_t key, hashtab_datum_t datum,
			   void *datap);
functions.description: Callback/utility to assign or record an index for a boolean symbol during hashtable traversal, storing results via datap. Supports building boolean index tables.
requirements: key and datum must correspond to a valid boolean symbol entry in the hashtable.
datap must be a non-NULL pointer to writable context/state required by the indexing routine (exact type is library-defined).
Caller must handle and check the returned int per the invoking table/iteration API.

functions.name: cond_read_bool
functions.signature: extern int cond_read_bool(policydb_t * p, hashtab_t h, struct policy_file *fp);
functions.description: Reads boolean symbols/definitions from a policy file into a hashtable in the context of the given policy database. Used during policy load or module import.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t ready to receive boolean entries.
h must be a valid hashtab_t instance for storing booleans.
fp must be a valid, open policy_file positioned at the boolean section to read.
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure and handle parse or I/O errors.

functions.name: cond_read_list
functions.signature: extern int cond_read_list(policydb_t * p, cond_list_t ** list, void *fp);
functions.description: Reads a list of conditional nodes/structures from a policy stream/file into a cond_list_t, attaching it to the provided output pointer. Used during parsing of conditional blocks.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized policydb_t.
list must be a non-NULL pointer to a cond_list_t* output variable; on success, *list is set to the newly read list that the caller must later destroy with cond_list_destroy().
fp must be a valid file/stream context compatible with the library’s policy reading functions (exact type is opaque here).
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cond_compute_av
functions.signature:
extern void cond_compute_av(avtab_t * ctab, avtab_key_t * key,
			    struct sepol_av_decision *avd);
functions.description: Computes an access vector decision given a conditional rule table and key, writing the result into avd. Incorporates conditional enablement state into the decision.
requirements: ctab must be a valid pointer to an avtab_t containing conditional rules.
key must be a non-NULL pointer to the rule lookup key.
avd must be a non-NULL pointer to writable sepol_av_decision storage to receive the computed decision.
Inputs must be initialized consistently with the current policy state (e.g., evaluate_conds run if required).

functions.name: constraint_expr_init
functions.description: Initializes a constraint_expr_t structure so it can be safely used in constraint expressions (e.g., sets fields to default/empty state and prepares internal containers like the ebitmap). Typical usage is to allocate a constraint_expr_t (stack or heap), call this initializer, populate fields, and later call constraint_expr_destroy to release internal resources. Return value is a status code; exact success/failure conventions are not documented here.
requirements: expr must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable constraint_expr_t storage provided by the caller.
The structure should be considered uninitialized prior to this call; after successful initialization, it may be populated by the caller.
Call constraint_expr_destroy on the same object to release any resources allocated during/after initialization to avoid memory leaks.
Thread-safety and reentrancy guarantees are not documented; do not share the same object across threads without external synchronization.
Exact meaning of the int return value is not specified in this header; callers should check the return and handle non-success status appropriately.

functions.name: constraint_expr_destroy
functions.description: Releases internal resources held by a constraint_expr_t previously initialized with constraint_expr_init (e.g., frees any dynamically allocated members such as name bitmaps or nested structures). Does not free the expr pointer itself. Typical usage: call after you are done with the expression to prevent memory leaks; the object may be re-initialized again if needed.
requirements: expr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a constraint_expr_t that has been successfully initialized (e.g., via constraint_expr_init) or otherwise set to a valid state expected by this function.
The function does not free the expr object itself; if it was heap-allocated, the caller remains responsible for freeing the enclosing constraint_expr_t after destroy returns.
After destruction, the object should not be used unless it is re-initialized.
Behavior for passing an uninitialized or partially-initialized object is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: mls_context_init
functions.description: Initialize only the MLS range of a security context. Internally calls mls_range_init(&c->range). Use this when you need a valid range in an otherwise existing context_struct_t; it does not modify user/role/type.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
c->range must be either uninitialized or safe to initialize; user/role/type are left unchanged.

functions.name: mls_context_cpy
functions.signature: static inline int mls_context_cpy(context_struct_t * dst, const context_struct_t * src)
functions.description: Copy the MLS range from src to dst. Scalar fields (user, role, type) are not touched. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure as propagated from mls_range_cpy.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
src must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized context_struct_t (its MLS range must be valid for mls_range_cpy).
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value (e.g., -1) indicates failure and dst->range may be partially modified depending on mls_range_cpy semantics.

functions.name: mls_context_cpy_low
functions.signature: static inline int mls_context_cpy_low(context_struct_t *dst, const context_struct_t *src)
functions.description: Set both low and high levels of dst->range to the low level of src->range (sens and categories). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure (propagated from ebitmap_cpy). On failure while copying the second level, the function destroys the first level's category bitmap to avoid leaking.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
src must be a non-NULL pointer whose range.level[0] (low level) is valid and initialized.
Callers must check the return value: 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
On failure, dst->range may be left with a destroyed or partially modified category bitmap; caller should be prepared to reinitialize or destroy dst->range if needed.

functions.name: mls_context_cpy_high
functions.signature: static inline int mls_context_cpy_high(context_struct_t *dst, const context_struct_t *src)
functions.description: Set both low and high levels of dst->range to the high level of src->range (sens and categories). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure (from ebitmap_cpy). If the second copy fails, the first level's category bitmap is destroyed to avoid leaking.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
src must be a non-NULL pointer whose range.level[1] (high level) is valid and initialized.
Callers must check the return value: 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
On failure, dst->range may be partially modified; caller should reinitialize/destroy dst->range if needed.

functions.name: mls_context_glblub
functions.signature: static inline int mls_context_glblub(context_struct_t *dst, const context_struct_t *c1, const context_struct_t *c2)
functions.description: Compute the GLB/LUB combination of the MLS ranges of c1 and c2 and store the result into dst->range by calling mls_range_glblub. Intended for merging two contexts’ MLS ranges under dominance/compatibility rules. Return value is that of mls_range_glblub (0 on success, non-zero/negative on error, per underlying implementation).
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
c1 and c2 must be non-NULL pointers with initialized/valid MLS ranges.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors according to mls_range_glblub’s contract (exact codes unspecified here).
dst->range may be modified only on success; behavior on failure follows mls_range_glblub semantics (unspecified here).

functions.name: mls_context_cmp
functions.signature: static inline int mls_context_cmp(const context_struct_t * c1, const context_struct_t * c2)
functions.description: Compare two contexts’ MLS ranges for equality. Returns 1 if both low and high levels (sens and categories) are equal (via mls_level_eq), otherwise 0. Does not compare user/role/type.
requirements: c1 and c2 must be non-NULL pointers to valid contexts whose MLS ranges are initialized.
Expect a boolean-like return: 1 for equal, 0 for not equal.

functions.name: mls_context_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and reinitialize the MLS range in c. Safe to call with NULL. Internally calls mls_range_destroy on c->range and then reinitializes the range with mls_context_init. Does not alter user/role/type.
requirements: c may be NULL (no-op).
If c is non-NULL, c->range must be in a state acceptable to mls_range_destroy (zero-initialized or previously initialized).
After return (when c is non-NULL), c->range is reinitialized; user/role/type remain unchanged.

functions.name: context_init
functions.description: Zero-initialize the entire context_struct_t via memset. Sets user/role/type to 0 and clears the MLS range to an all-zero state. Use as the initial setup for a fresh context object.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
This performs a raw zeroing; it does not call mls_range_init. The MLS range implementation must tolerate zero-initialized state (as assumed by the rest of this header).

functions.name: context_cpy
functions.signature: static inline int context_cpy(context_struct_t * dst, const context_struct_t * src)
functions.description: Copy the full security context from src to dst: user, role, and type are copied directly; the MLS range is copied via mls_context_cpy. Returns 0 on success or a negative/non-zero error code from mls_context_cpy on failure.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable context_struct_t.
src must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized context_struct_t.
Callers must check the return value; on failure, dst may have user/role/type already copied while the MLS range copy failed.

functions.name: context_destroy
functions.description: Reset user/role/type to 0 and destroy+reinitialize the MLS range by delegating to mls_context_destroy. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: c may be NULL (no-op).
If c is non-NULL, it must be safe to call mls_context_destroy on c (its range zero-initialized or previously initialized).
After return (when c is non-NULL), user/role/type are 0 and c->range is reinitialized.

functions.name: context_cmp
functions.signature: static inline int context_cmp(const context_struct_t * c1, const context_struct_t * c2)
functions.description: Compare two contexts for full equality: user, role, type must match and the MLS ranges must be equal (via mls_context_cmp). Returns 1 if equal, otherwise 0.
requirements: c1 and c2 must be non-NULL pointers to valid contexts.
MLS ranges of both contexts must be in a valid, comparable state (initialized).
Expect a boolean-like return: 1 for equal, 0 for not equal.

functions.name: ebitmap_start
functions.signature: static inline unsigned int ebitmap_start(const ebitmap_t * e, ebitmap_node_t ** n)
functions.description: Initialize an iteration over an extensible bitmap by setting *n to the first node of e and returning the starting bit index for the iteration. Typically used with ebitmap_next and ebitmap_node_get_bit (or the provided iteration macros).
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an ebitmap_t (may be empty).
n must be a valid, non-null pointer to an ebitmap_node_t* variable.
If e is empty (e->node == NULL), the returned bit index will equal ebitmap_length(e) (0), resulting in no iteration steps.

functions.name: ebitmap_init
functions.description: Zero-initialize an extensible bitmap structure so it starts empty and in a known state.
requirements: e must be a valid, non-null pointer to an ebitmap_t.
After initialization, ebitmap_destroy can be safely called on e.

functions.name: ebitmap_next
functions.signature: static inline unsigned int ebitmap_next(ebitmap_node_t ** n, unsigned int bit)
functions.description: Advance an iteration over the bitmap. If bit is the last bit covered by the current node and a next node exists, *n is advanced to the next node and its startbit is returned; otherwise returns bit + 1.
requirements: n must be a valid, non-null pointer to an ebitmap_node_t* and *n must point to a valid node.
bit is expected to be within the current node’s covered range [(*n)->startbit, (*n)->startbit + MAPSIZE - 1] when used for in-node iteration.
When bit equals ((*n)->startbit + MAPSIZE - 1) and (*n)->next is NULL, the function still returns bit + 1; callers must bound iteration using ebitmap_length(e).

functions.name: ebitmap_node_get_bit
functions.signature: static inline int ebitmap_node_get_bit(const ebitmap_node_t * n, unsigned int bit)
functions.description: Test whether a specific bit within the given node’s map is set. Returns 1 if the bit is set, 0 otherwise.
requirements: n must be a valid, non-null pointer to an ebitmap_node_t.

Should be called before using level with ebitmap operations or before passing to other MLS helpers.

functions.name: mls_level_destroy
functions.description: Destroys and reinitializes an mls_level by freeing its category bitmap via ebitmap_destroy and then zero-initializing the structure. Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
requirements: If level is non-NULL, it must either be uninitialized/zeroed or have a category bitmap previously placed in a state acceptable to ebitmap_destroy (e.g., initialized by mls_level_init or populated by other MLS routines).
After return, level is reset to an initialized zero state.

functions.name: mls_level_eq
functions.signature: static inline int mls_level_eq(const struct mls_level *l1, const struct mls_level *l2)
functions.description: Compares two MLS levels for equality. Returns non-zero if both the sensitivity and category sets are equal (via ebitmap_cmp), otherwise 0. Does not modify inputs.
requirements: l1 and l2 must be non-NULL and refer to initialized mls_level objects whose cat bitmaps are valid for comparison.

functions.name: mls_level_dom
functions.signature: static inline int mls_level_dom(const struct mls_level *l1, const struct mls_level *l2)
functions.description: Checks whether MLS level l1 dominates l2: l1->sens >= l2->sens and l1’s category set contains l2’s category set (via ebitmap_contains). Returns non-zero if l1 dominates l2, else 0.
requirements: l1 and l2 must be non-NULL and refer to initialized mls_level objects with valid cat bitmaps.

functions.name: mls_range_cpy
functions.signature: static inline int mls_range_cpy(mls_range_t *dst, const mls_range_t *src)
functions.description: Copies an MLS range from src to dst by copying both low (level[0]) and high (level[1]) levels using mls_level_cpy. On failure when copying the high level, it destroys the already-copied low level in dst and returns -1. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: dst and src must be non-NULL pointers to mls_range objects.
src must be initialized; both src->level[0] and src->level[1] must have valid cat bitmaps.
dst levels should be in a state acceptable to mls_level_cpy (typically initialized via mls_range_init).
Caller must check the return value; on -1, dst->level[0] has been destroyed and dst is left partially reset.

functions.name: mls_range_init
functions.description: Initializes an MLS range by initializing both low and high levels via mls_level_init. Prepares the range for subsequent operations or destruction.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: mls_range_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an MLS range by destroying both low and high levels via mls_level_destroy. Leaves the levels reinitialized to zeroed state.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to an mls_range previously initialized (directly or via use with MLS helpers).

functions.name: mls_range_eq
functions.signature: static inline int mls_range_eq(const struct mls_range *r1, const struct mls_range *r2)
functions.description: Compares two MLS ranges for equality by checking equality of both low and high levels via mls_level_eq. Returns non-zero if equal, otherwise 0.
requirements: r1 and r2 must be non-NULL and refer to initialized mls_range objects with valid levels and cat bitmaps.

functions.name: mls_semantic_cat_init

requirements: c must be a valid non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: mls_semantic_cat_destroy
functions.description: Destroys or clears resources associated with an mls_semantic_cat_t. Exact behavior is not documented here; likely frees any linked list nodes and resets fields.
requirements: c must be a valid pointer, previously initialized (e.g., via mls_semantic_cat_init) or populated by related APIs.
Caller must not use c’s internal resources after destruction unless reinitialized.

functions.name: mls_semantic_level_init
functions.description: Initializes a semantic MLS level (sensitivity and associated semantic categories). Details are not provided here; likely zeroes sens and sets cat list to NULL.
requirements: l must be a valid non-NULL pointer.
Should be called before using l with other semantic range/level functions.

functions.name: mls_semantic_level_destroy
functions.description: Destroys or clears resources associated with a semantic MLS level, including any linked category structures. Details are not provided in this header.
requirements: l must be a valid pointer, previously initialized or populated by related APIs.
After destruction, l should be considered uninitialized until reinitialized.

functions.name: mls_semantic_level_cpy
functions.description: Copies a semantic MLS level from src to dst. The header does not document semantics; typical behavior would duplicate sensitivity value and the category list. Returns an int status (0 on success, negative on failure is typical but not specified here).
requirements: dst and src must be non-NULL pointers.
src should reference an initialized semantic level; dst should be initialized and in a state acceptable for copy (to avoid leaks).
Caller must check the return value and handle potential partial copies if an error is reported (details unspecified).

functions.name: mls_semantic_range_init
functions.description: Initializes a semantic MLS range (low/high semantic levels). Details are not provided; likely initializes both levels and associated lists to default/empty values.
requirements: r must be a valid non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: mls_semantic_range_destroy
functions.description: Destroys resources associated with a semantic MLS range, likely destroying both low and high semantic levels and any linked category lists.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer, previously initialized or populated by related APIs.
After destruction, the object should be considered uninitialized until reinitialized.

functions.name: mls_semantic_range_cpy
functions.description: Copies a semantic MLS range from src to dst. Specific copy semantics are not documented here; typical behavior would deep-copy both low and high semantic levels including category lists. Returns an int status (value conventions not specified).
requirements: dst and src must be non-NULL pointers.
src should be initialized; dst should be initialized and prepared to receive a deep copy to avoid resource leaks.
Caller must check the return value and handle potential partial-copy states if an error occurs (details unspecified).

functions.name: sepol_module_package_init

requirements: p must be a non-null pointer to a writable sepol_module_package_t instance.
The pointed-to object must be valid storage (not read-only) for the duration of the call.
Callers should check the integer return value to determine success or failure; the specific success/failure conventions (e.g., 0 on success) are not documented here and are unknown.
If the function reports failure, the post-call state of *p is unspecified; callers should not assume the structure is initialized.

functions.name: sepol_polcap_getnum
functions.description: Converts a SELinux policy capability name to its numeric identifier. Intended for looking up the enum/index of a capability by its textual name as used in policy. Returns an integer code corresponding to a policy capability; exact return semantics for unknown names are not documented here. Typical usage: pass a NUL-terminated capability name and use the returned number with other policy-cap APIs.
requirements: name must point to a valid, NUL-terminated string (inferred from const char* parameter).
name should correspond to a known policy capability name recognized by the library; otherwise the result may indicate an error or an unknown mapping (behavior not documented here).
The caller must not pass an invalid pointer (must be readable for the string length).
Thread-safety and error conventions are not documented; callers should not assume global state changes (unknown).

functions.name: sepol_polcap_getname
functions.description: Converts a SELinux policy capability number to its canonical name string. Intended for retrieving the textual name for a capability enumerated in the policy. Returns a pointer to a constant string for the given capability number; behavior for out-of-range values is not documented here and may return NULL or another sentinel.
requirements: capnum should be a valid capability index in the range [0, POLICYDB_CAP_MAX] (inferred from the enum and POLICYDB_CAP_MAX).
The returned pointer refers to immutable storage; the caller must not modify or free it (inferred from const char* return).
If capnum is out of range or unknown, the function may return NULL (behavior not specified; callers should defensively check for NULL).
Thread-safety and lifetime of returned strings are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: policydb_init

requirements: p must be a non-null pointer to policydb_t storage that the caller owns.

On success, the returned int is 0 (POLICYDB_SUCCESS); negative values indicate error (per header constants).

functions.name: policydb_from_image

functions.description: Parses a binary policy image in memory and populates the provided policydb_t with the parsed policy.
requirements: handle may be used for reporting; if provided, it must be a valid sepol_handle_t pointer (may be NULL if the API allows; not specified).
data must point to a buffer containing the policy image and remain valid for the duration of the call.
len must be the size in bytes of the policy image buffer at data.
policydb must be a non-null pointer to an initialized policydb_t (e.g., by policydb_init).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: policydb_to_image
functions.signature: extern int policydb_to_image(sepol_handle_t * handle, policydb_t * policydb, void **newdata, size_t * newlen);
functions.description: Serializes a policydb_t into a newly allocated binary policy image in memory.
requirements: handle may be used for reporting; if provided, it must be a valid sepol_handle_t pointer (not specified whether NULL is allowed).
policydb must be a non-null pointer to an initialized and populated policy database.
newdata must be a non-null pointer to a void* output location; on success it will receive a pointer to allocated memory containing the image.
newlen must be a non-null pointer to receive the size in bytes of the generated image.
Caller is responsible for freeing the buffer returned via *newdata using the appropriate allocator for this library (exact function unspecified here).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: policydb_index_classes

functions.description: Indexes non-class/boolean symbols and other policy structures. Intended for finalizing indexes after reading or linking a policy.
requirements: handle may be used for reporting; it should be a valid sepol_handle_t if non-NULL.
