Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid concurrent mutation of the supplied policydb while service functions are executing.

functions.name: sepol_set_sidtab
functions.description: Registers a caller-supplied SID table (sidtab_t) for use by libsepol service functions rather than the internal default. Enables direct management of SID mappings by the caller.
requirements: s must point to a valid, initialized sidtab_t and remain valid for the lifetime of subsequent service operations that use it.
Call before other service functions that should use the provided sidtab.
Avoid concurrent modification of the supplied sidtab while service functions run; thread-safety unspecified.

functions.name: sepol_load_policy
functions.description: Loads and initializes the policydb and sidtab from a binary policy image provided by the caller. Sets up the internal state needed for access vector computations and SID operations.
requirements: data must point to a readable buffer containing a complete binary SELinux policy image of exactly len bytes.
len must match the size of the binary policy image; must be non-zero.
Must be called (directly or via other setup) before functions that require an initialized policy if the policydb/sidtab have not already been set or initialized.
The buffer need only remain valid for the duration of this call.

functions.name: sepol_compute_av
functions.signature: extern int sepol_compute_av(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_access_vector_t requested, struct sepol_av_decision *avd);
functions.description: Computes the access vector decision for a subject SID (ssid) accessing a target SID (tsid) for the given class (tclass). Evaluates requested permission bits and fills avd with the decision (allowed/denied and related fields).
requirements: avd must be a valid non-null pointer to a writable sepol_av_decision structure.
tclass must be a valid security class known to the loaded policy.
requested is a bitmask of permissions for tclass; bits outside the class’s defined permissions are unspecified.
The policy must be loaded/initialized before calling.

functions.name: sepol_compute_av_reason
functions.signature: extern int sepol_compute_av_reason(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_access_vector_t requested, struct sepol_av_decision *avd, unsigned int *reason);
functions.description: Like sepol_compute_av, but also returns bitwise reasons for any denials (and potentially sources of allow) via reason. Reason bits may include TE, constraints, RBAC, and bounds (see SEPOL_COMPUTEAV_* flags).
requirements: avd must be a valid non-null pointer to a writable sepol_av_decision.
reason must be a valid non-null pointer to an unsigned int to receive reason flags.
tclass must be a valid class; requested is a permission bitmask for that class.
Policy must be loaded/initialized prior to call.

functions.name: sepol_compute_av_reason_buffer
functions.signature: extern int sepol_compute_av_reason_buffer(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_access_vector_t requested, struct sepol_av_decision *avd, unsigned int *reason, char **reason_buf, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Extends sepol_compute_av_reason by also returning a dynamically allocated, human-readable buffer describing constraint expression evaluations (denied by default; include granted when flags has SHOW_GRANTED). Caller must free the buffer with free(3).
requirements: avd must be a non-null pointer to writable sepol_av_decision.
reason must be a non-null pointer to unsigned int for reason flags.
reason_buf must be a non-null pointer; on success, *reason_buf points to malloc’d memory that the caller must free with free(3).
flags may include SHOW_GRANTED to include granted constraints; other flag semantics unspecified.
tclass must be valid; requested is a permission bitmask for that class.
Policy must be loaded/initialized before calling.

functions.name: sepol_validate_transition_reason_buffer
functions.signature: extern int sepol_validate_transition_reason_buffer(sepol_security_id_t oldsid, sepol_security_id_t newsid, sepol_security_id_t tasksid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, char **reason_buf, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Evaluates MLS/validatetrans constraints for a proposed label transition from oldsid to newsid by a task with tasksid for objects of class tclass. Returns a dynamically allocated buffer describing the constraint calculations; by default shows denied constraints, or both granted and denied when flags includes SHOW_GRANTED.
requirements: reason_buf must be non-null; on success, *reason_buf points to malloc’d memory that must be freed with free(3).
flags may include SHOW_GRANTED; other flags unspecified.
tclass must be a valid security class.
Policy must be loaded/initialized before calling.

functions.name: sepol_string_to_security_class
functions.description: Maps a class name string to its corresponding security class ID.
requirements: class_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string naming a known security class.
tclass must be a non-null pointer to receive the class ID.
Policy or class metadata must be initialized/available (via loaded policy).

functions.name: sepol_string_to_av_perm
functions.signature: extern int sepol_string_to_av_perm(sepol_security_class_t tclass, const char *perm_name, sepol_access_vector_t *av);
functions.description: Maps a permission name string, scoped to a given class tclass, to its corresponding access vector bit.
requirements: tclass must be a valid security class ID.
perm_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string naming a permission within tclass.
av must be a non-null pointer to receive the permission bit.
Requires that class/permission metadata be available from the loaded policy.

functions.name: sepol_av_perm_to_string
functions.signature: extern const char *sepol_av_perm_to_string(sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_access_vector_t av);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an internal string buffer containing the permission name corresponding to the given class and permission bit. The returned buffer is internal and will be overwritten by the next call to this function or sepol_av_to_string(). Copy the string if persistence is needed.
requirements: tclass must be a valid security class.
av must specify a single permission bit valid for tclass; behavior for multiple/invalid bits is unspecified.
Caller must not free the returned pointer and must copy it if it needs to persist beyond the next related call.

functions.name: sepol_transition_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_transition_sid(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Computes the SID to label a newly created object of class tclass given subject and target SIDs. Returns the resulting SID via out_sid.
requirements: out_sid must be a non-null pointer to receive the computed SID.
tclass must be a valid object class known to the policy.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.
ssid and tsid must be valid SIDs for the loaded policy.

functions.name: sepol_member_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_member_sid(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Computes the SID for selecting a member of a polyinstantiated object of class tclass based on a subject/target SID pair. Returns the resulting SID via out_sid.
requirements: out_sid must be non-null.
tclass must be valid.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.
ssid and tsid must be valid SIDs.

functions.name: sepol_change_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_change_sid(sepol_security_id_t ssid, sepol_security_id_t tsid, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Computes the SID to use when relabeling an existing object of class tclass based on subject and target SIDs. Returns the resulting SID via out_sid.
requirements: out_sid must be non-null.
tclass must be valid.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.
ssid and tsid must be valid SIDs.

functions.name: sepol_sid_to_context
functions.signature: extern int sepol_sid_to_context(sepol_security_id_t sid, sepol_security_context_t * scontext, size_t * scontext_len);
functions.description: Converts a SID to its security context string, allocating a string of the correct size and returning it via scontext along with its length in scontext_len. Caller must free the returned string with free(3).
requirements: scontext must be non-null; on success, *scontext points to malloc’d memory that the caller must free with free(3).
scontext_len must be a non-null pointer to receive the length of the returned string.
sid must be a valid SID for the loaded policy.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_context_to_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_context_to_sid(sepol_const_security_context_t scontext, size_t scontext_len, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Converts a security context string (and its length) to the corresponding SID, returning it via out_sid.
requirements: scontext must point to a readable context buffer of length scontext_len; it may be NUL-terminated but the function relies on the provided length.
scontext_len must be the actual number of bytes of the context string.
out_sid must be a non-null pointer to receive the SID.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_get_user_sids
functions.signature: extern int sepol_get_user_sids(sepol_security_id_t callsid, char *username, sepol_security_id_t ** sids, uint32_t * nel);
functions.description: Generates the set of SIDs for legal security contexts for a given user that are reachable from callsid. Returns a dynamically allocated array of SIDs via sids and the count via nel. Caller is responsible for freeing the array with free(3).
requirements: username must be a non-null, NUL-terminated user name known to the policy.
sids must be non-null; on success, *sids points to malloc’d memory that the caller must free with free(3).
nel must be a non-null pointer to receive the number of SIDs returned.
callsid must be a valid SID for the loaded policy.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_fs_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_fs_sid(char *dev, sepol_security_id_t * fs_sid, sepol_security_id_t * file_sid);
functions.description: Returns the SIDs to use for an unlabeled filesystem being mounted from device dev: fs_sid for the filesystem object and file_sid for files within that filesystem.
requirements: dev must be a non-null, NUL-terminated device name string (e.g., kdevname).
fs_sid and file_sid must be non-null pointers to receive SIDs.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_port_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_port_sid(uint16_t domain, uint16_t type, uint8_t protocol, uint16_t port, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Returns the SID associated with a network port identified by address family (domain), socket type, protocol, and port number.
requirements: out_sid must be non-null.
domain, type, and protocol must be valid and consistent (e.g., as used in socket APIs); port is the transport-layer port number for the given protocol.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_ibpkey_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_ibpkey_sid(uint64_t subnet_prefix_p, uint16_t pkey, sepol_security_id_t *out_sid);
functions.description: Returns the SID associated with an InfiniBand partition key (pkey) within a given subnet prefix.
requirements: out_sid must be non-null.
subnet_prefix_p and pkey must be valid identifiers for the target InfiniBand fabric.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_ibendport_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_ibendport_sid(char *dev_name, uint8_t port, sepol_security_id_t *out_sid);
functions.description: Returns the SID associated with an InfiniBand end port identified by device name and port number.
requirements: dev_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated device name string.
out_sid must be non-null.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_netif_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_netif_sid(char *name, sepol_security_id_t * if_sid, sepol_security_id_t * msg_sid);
functions.description: Returns SIDs for a network interface identified by name: if_sid for the interface itself and msg_sid as the default SID for messages received on that interface.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated interface name string.
if_sid and msg_sid must be non-null pointers to receive SIDs.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_node_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_node_sid(uint16_t domain, void *addr, size_t addrlen, sepol_security_id_t * out_sid);
functions.description: Returns the SID associated with a network node (host) identified by an address in the specified address family (domain). addr points to the binary address of length addrlen bytes.
requirements: addr must point to a readable buffer of exactly addrlen bytes representing an address for the given domain (e.g., struct in_addr or in6_addr bytes).
out_sid must be non-null.
domain must be a valid address family identifier matching the format of addr.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_fs_use
functions.signature: extern int sepol_fs_use(const char *fstype, unsigned int *behavior, sepol_security_id_t * sid);
functions.description: Determines how SELinux labeling should be handled for the given filesystem type. Returns a behavior code (SECURITY_FS_USE_*) and optionally a SID for the filesystem object.
requirements: fstype must be a non-null, NUL-terminated filesystem type string.
behavior must be a non-null pointer to receive one of SECURITY_FS_USE_XATTR, SECURITY_FS_USE_TRANS, SECURITY_FS_USE_TASK, SECURITY_FS_USE_GENFS, or SECURITY_FS_USE_NONE.
sid may be non-null to receive a filesystem SID when applicable.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_genfs_sid
functions.signature: extern int sepol_genfs_sid(const char *fstype, const char *name, sepol_security_class_t sclass, sepol_security_id_t * sid);
functions.description: Returns the SID to use for a file in a filesystem that cannot support persistent labels or other fixed-labeling behaviors. Uses genfs labeling rules for the given filesystem type, object name/path, and security class.
requirements: fstype must be a non-null, NUL-terminated filesystem type string.
name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated name/path relevant to the genfs rule lookup.
sclass must be a valid security class for the object.
sid must be a non-null pointer to receive the resulting SID.
Policy must be loaded/initialized.

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_init
functions.description: Initialize a sidtab_t instance for use. Sets up the internal hash table, counters, and bookkeeping so entries can be inserted/searched. Call before any other sidtab operations on the object.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to sidtab_t.
s must point to storage the caller controls; it will be initialized by this function.
Must be called before using s with insert/search/map/etc.
Return value is an int status code; the caller must check it for failure (exact convention unknown).

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_insert
functions.signature: int sepol_sidtab_insert(sidtab_t * s, sepol_security_id_t sid, context_struct_t * context);
functions.description: Insert or register a mapping from the given security identifier (sid) to the provided security context into the sidtab. Intended for populating the table with known SID→context associations.
requirements: s must be a non-null, previously initialized sidtab_t (via sepol_sidtab_init).
context must be a non-null pointer to a valid/initialized context_struct_t.
sid must be a value of type sepol_security_id_t; any uniqueness/validity constraints are unknown from this header.
May fail and return a non-success status; the caller must check the return value (exact convention unknown).

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_search
functions.description: Look up the security context associated with the given sid in the sidtab. Returns a pointer to the stored context, or possibly NULL if not found (exact behavior unknown).
requirements: s must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
sid must be a value of type sepol_security_id_t.
Returned pointer, if non-null, refers to an internal context entry owned by the table; lifetime/ownership semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_map
functions.signature: int sepol_sidtab_map(sidtab_t * s, int (*apply)(sepol_security_id_t sid, context_struct_t * context, void *args), void *args);
functions.description: Iterate over entries in the sidtab and invoke the user-supplied apply callback for each (sid, context) pair, passing through args. Useful for traversal, inspection, or bulk operations.
requirements: s must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
apply must be a non-null function pointer with signature int(sepol_security_id_t, context_struct_t *, void *).
The callback must tolerate being called multiple times and must not invalidate or free the sidtab’s internal data unless explicitly intended; exact mutation rules are not specified.
args is an opaque pointer passed to each callback invocation and may be NULL.
The function returns an int status; callers must check for errors (exact convention unknown).

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_map_remove_on_error
functions.signature: void sepol_sidtab_map_remove_on_error(sidtab_t * s, int (*apply)(sepol_security_id_t s, context_struct_t * context, void *args), void *args);
functions.description: Iterate over sidtab entries calling apply for each. According to the name, entries for which the callback signals an error are removed from the table; exact error signaling semantics are not documented here.
requirements: s must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
apply must be a non-null function pointer with signature int(sepol_security_id_t, context_struct_t *, void *).
The callback should return a value indicating success or error; the exact convention (e.g., nonzero = error) is not specified here.
The callback must not access entries after they have been removed; specifics of removal timing are not documented.
args is an opaque pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_context_to_sid
functions.signature: int sepol_sidtab_context_to_sid(sidtab_t * s, context_struct_t * context, sepol_security_id_t * sid);
functions.description: Resolve or allocate the security identifier corresponding to the provided security context. On success, writes the SID to *sid. Commonly used to look up existing mappings or assign a new SID for a context.
requirements: s must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
context must be a non-null pointer to a valid/initialized context_struct_t.
sid must be a non-null pointer to storage where the resulting sepol_security_id_t will be written.
Returns an int status; the caller must check for failure and must not use *sid on failure (exact status convention unknown).

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_hash_eval
functions.description: Evaluate and report characteristics of the sidtab’s hash table (e.g., distribution), likely for debugging or diagnostics. The tag string can label the output. Behavior/outputs are not defined here.
requirements: h must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
tag should be a non-null, NUL-terminated string label; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_destroy
functions.description: Tear down and free resources associated with a sidtab, invalidating it for further use. After destruction, the table should not be used unless re-initialized.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a sidtab_t previously initialized with sepol_sidtab_init.
All outstanding uses of pointers returned by the table (e.g., from search) must be ceased before destruction; exact ownership semantics of those pointers are not documented.
Must not be called concurrently with other operations on the same sidtab (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_set
functions.description: Set dst to the state of src. Likely copies or assigns the sidtab contents and metadata from src to dst; whether this is a deep copy, shallow assignment, or move is not specified.
requirements: dst must be a non-null pointer to a sidtab_t.
src must be a non-null pointer to a sidtab_t, presumably initialized.
After the call, usage/ownership semantics of src and dst are not specified; callers should avoid double-free or concurrent mutation until semantics are confirmed.

functions.name: sepol_sidtab_shutdown
functions.description: Mark the sidtab as shutting down, preventing or altering further modifications. Typically used during teardown to stop new inserts; exact effects are not specified here.
requirements: s must be a non-null, initialized sidtab_t.
After shutdown, callers should avoid operations that mutate the table; exact allowed operations are not documented.

functions.name: symtab_init
functions.description: Initializes a symbol table (symtab) that maps string keys to arbitrary datum values, internally backed by a hash table. Call this before any operations that rely on the table. The size parameter specifies the initial hash table size (number of buckets). Return value semantics are not documented here; callers should check the integer result to detect initialization failure.
requirements: symtab must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a symtab_t structure.
symtab must not already be initialized when passed to this function (inferred from typical init/destroy patterns).
size specifies the initial hash table size; no explicit range is documented here, but typical usage provides a positive, non-zero value (inferred).
Callers must check the returned int for success/failure; exact success value is not documented in this header (unknown).
Resources allocated by a successful call must later be released with symtab_destroy(symtab).

functions.name: symtab_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a previously initialized symtab and releases any resources it holds. After this call, the symtab must not be used again unless re-initialized.
requirements: symtab must be a non-null pointer to a symtab_t that has been successfully initialized by symtab_init (inferred).
Do not call this function more than once on the same symtab without re-initializing it (inferred).
After this call, the symtab must not be accessed or used until it is re-initialized.

functions.name: add_i_to_a
functions.description: Adds a 32-bit unsigned integer value i to an array a, updating the element count cnt, typically allocating or resizing the underlying array as needed. Intended as a small utility for building or extending uint32_t arrays. Allocation strategy, ordering, and duplicate handling are not documented; details are unknown.
requirements: cnt must be a valid, non-null pointer to the array element count associated with *a.
a must be a valid, non-null pointer to a modifiable uint32_t*; the function may update *a to point to a (re)allocated buffer.
If the function reallocates the array, any previous value of *a may become invalid; use only the updated *a after the call.
The interpretation of the return value is not documented; success/failure conventions are unknown.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified.

functions.name: sepol_av_to_string
functions.signature: char *sepol_av_to_string(const policydb_t *policydbp, sepol_security_class_t tclass, sepol_access_vector_t av);
functions.description: Converts a security access vector av for a given object class tclass into a human-readable string using the provided SELinux policy database. Useful for logging, diagnostics, or presenting permissions. Memory ownership and formatting details are not documented; whether the caller must free the returned string is unknown.
requirements: policydbp must be a valid, initialized policydb_t pointer corresponding to the policy used for interpretation.
tclass must be a valid security class defined in policydbp; passing an invalid class leads to undefined behavior or errors (exact behavior unknown).
av must be a valid access vector bitmask for the specified class; exact valid bits are policy-defined.
The returned char* must be treated as read-only; whether it must be freed by the caller is not documented (ownership unknown).
Thread-safety relative to the policy database and any internal buffers is unspecified.

functions.name: sepol_extended_perms_to_string
functions.description: Converts extended permission data xperms into a human-readable string. Intended to assist with diagnostics or logging of extended permissions. Exact formatting and memory ownership are not documented; whether the caller must free the returned string is unknown.
requirements: xperms must be a valid, non-null pointer to an avtab_extended_perms_t structure.
The returned char* must be treated as read-only; whether it must be freed by the caller is not documented (ownership unknown).
Thread-safety is unspecified.

functions.name: tokenize
functions.signature: int tokenize(const char *line_buf, char delim, int num_args, ...);
functions.description: Splits the input C string line_buf into tokens separated by the delimiter delim and writes parsed values into the provided variadic output arguments, serving as a lightweight replacement for sscanf. Specific expected types, conversion rules, and error conventions are not documented and are unknown.
requirements: line_buf must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
num_args must be non-negative and must exactly match the number of variadic output arguments provided.
Each variadic argument must be a valid pointer to writable storage of the type expected by tokenize for the corresponding token; the exact expected types and conversions are not documented (unknown).
delim specifies the single-character delimiter used to split tokens; behavior with consecutive delimiters or empty tokens is not documented (unknown).
The meaning of the return value (e.g., number of tokens parsed vs. error codes) is not documented (unknown).
Behavior with input lines containing fewer or more tokens than num_args is not documented (unknown).

data_types.description: Raw binary SELinux policy image (policy.kern/base/mod) as produced by checkpolicy or semodule packaging. Opaque binary format consumed by libsepol/policydb readers.
A file on disk whose contents are a binary SELinux policy image. The filename itself is irrelevant; the data read from the file should be a valid binary policy image.
A textual SELinux security context in the form user:role:type[:range], optionally including an MLS range component.
Text representing an MLS sensitivity/category level or range per SELinux syntax, e.g., s0-s0:c0.c1023 or s0:c0,c3.
Textual file_contexts content mapping path regexes to SELinux contexts, typically lines like '/path regex  system_u:object_r:type_t:s0'.
Text mapping Linux usernames to SELinux users and MLS ranges, e.g., 'user: seuser:mlsrange' lines as in /etc/selinux/*/seusers.
Additional SELinux user configuration blob used by libsepol/semodule packaging; free-form text in formats expected by SELinux tools.
Textual netfilter (iptables/nftables) context mappings used by SELinux, specifying contexts for netfilter objects.
An arbitrary NUL-terminated string with no specific required format; used here for names where format constraints are not enforced in the stub.
A single identifier naming an SELinux role (alphanumeric and underscores by convention), e.g., 'staff_r', without additional separators or context components.

An arbitrary sequence of bytes sourced from a string buffer (not interpreted as text). Used when APIs expect a pointer to a byte array and an explicit length, e.g., network addresses or masks (4 or 16 bytes). The content may include any byte values including NUL and is not required to be UTF-8 or printable.
